name: Raindrop.io

pricing.notes: The free plan offers unlimited bookmarks, collections, and devices, with up to 3 highlights per bookmark and 100 MB/month uploads. Pro adds full-text search, Stella AI save-time tag and collection suggestions, permanent page copies, reminders, annotations (unlimited highlights in 4 colors with notes), and daily backups. Yearly billing is about 20% cheaper than monthly.

pros: One of the most generous free plans anywhere: unlimited bookmarks, collections, and up to 3 highlights per bookmark
Polished apps on every platform — web, Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS, Android, and all major browser extensions
Strong visual organization with covers, nested collections, and multiple view modes
Public collections make sharing a curated list as easy as sending a link
Pro is cheap at $28/year and adds permanent copies of saved pages plus daily backups
Open API and 2,600+ integrations via services like Zapier and IFTTT
cons: Search is keyword-based — no semantic search, so you need to remember titles, tags, or exact words
AI is limited to save-time tag and collection suggestions (Stella) on Pro; no automatic tagging across saves, no summaries, no chat, no YouTube features
Full-text search and annotations (beyond 3 highlights/bookmark) are paywalled behind Pro
Reading experience is basic compared to dedicated read-it-later apps, with no true offline mode
bestFor: Collectors and visual organizers who file thousands of bookmarks into structured collections and want polished apps everywhere without paying.
verdict: The best traditional bookmark filing cabinet — organization is world-class, but finding things still depends on your own tags and keywords.
overview: Raindrop.io is a bookmark manager that has been in continuous development since 2013 and is widely treated as the benchmark for organizing links at scale. Bookmarks live in nested collections with cover art, tags, and several view modes, and the free plan is unusually generous: unlimited bookmarks, collections, up to 3 highlights per bookmark, and devices, plus import and export. Apps cover the web, Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android, with extensions for Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge, and other major browsers. The Pro plan — about $28 a year ($3.25/mo direct) — adds full-text search across saved pages and PDFs, an AI assistant (Stella) that suggests tags and collections at save time, permanent archived copies of pages, annotations, reminders, a duplicate finder, and daily backups. Collections can be shared publicly or used collaboratively, and a documented API plus thousands of integrations make it easy to wire into other tools. Raindrop imports from Pocket, browser bookmark HTML files, and most competing services.

faqs.a: Yes — Raindrop.io has one of the most generous free plans in the category: unlimited bookmarks, collections, and devices with up to 3 highlights per bookmark, plus import and export. The paid Pro plan costs about $28/year (or $3.25/month direct, $27.99/year on the App Store) and adds full-text search, Stella AI tag suggestions, permanent copies of saved pages, annotations, reminders, and daily backups.

Yes. Raindrop.io is actively maintained and remains one of the most popular bookmark managers, especially after Pocket shut down in July 2025. It has been developed continuously since 2013, ships apps for web, Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS, and Android plus all major browser extensions, and continues to receive regular feature updates.

faqs.q: What is the best Raindrop.io alternative?
faqs.a: The best Raindrop.io alternative in 2026 is Marqly if you want an AI-first bookmark manager that solves Raindrop's biggest friction point: manual tagging and keyword search. With Marqly, you find saves by describing what you remember (semantic search), get automatic AI summaries of articles and YouTube videos, and can chat directly with your saved content. For open-source self-hosting, Linkwarden or Karakeep are solid alternatives; for dedicated long-form reading queues, Readwise Reader or Instapaper.

faqs.q: How do I switch from Raindrop.io to Marqly?
faqs.a: Switching from Raindrop to Marqly takes under two minutes: in Raindrop, go to Settings → Backups and click Export HTML. Then log in to Marqly, open Settings → Import, and upload your Raindrop file. Marqly preserves your collections, extracts full content, and runs AI auto-tagging so your entire library becomes searchable by meaning.

Yes. Raindrop.io has a native iOS app with share-sheet saving, collections, tags, and highlights, and it syncs with the web app and browser extensions. Pro pricing through the App Store is $2.99/month or $27.99/year. Saved pages are cached, but there is no dedicated offline reading mode like a read-it-later app.

faqs.q: Can I export my data from Raindrop.io?
faqs.a: Yes, and export is available on the free plan. Raindrop.io exports your bookmarks as HTML or CSV files, which nearly every bookmark manager can import — Marqly, for example, has a dedicated Raindrop import. Pro subscribers additionally get automatic daily backups of their library. There is no lock-in; a full export takes about a minute.
